beats.text: A visitor offers samples, a poster, and a gift at the BHS. Mimi asks: What is the product and expected return? She pauses acceptance.
The two policies have different scopes: covered breastmilk substitutes and related products under the Milk Code; prescription products and medical devices under the pharmaceutical order.
Mimi checks four details: product, promotion, place and audience, and inducement. Free is not authorization. Prescription samples cannot be distributed to the public.
Mimi says: I will not accept or distribute these items. I will refer the details to the supervisor. She cannot approve an exception independently.
Mimi uses approved information without brand endorsement. Reports contain facts, without patient data. Do not blame families; refer clinical questions to a health professional.
A promotional gift and an educational model differ. Verify the rules: recognize, pause, and refer. An educational label is insufficient; the BHW does not approve independently.
